title: Cessna 150 M — Emergency Procedures (independently worded)
description: Emergency procedure checklist for the Cessna 150 M with Lycoming O-235 engine. Memory items are marked and must be performed before consulting this list. No airspeeds, power settings, or other numerical limitations are stated — those must come from the specific aircraft's POH. Verify all items against the actual aircraft before flight.

source.notes: No manufacturer document was consulted or copied. This file was authored from general familiarity with the Cessna 150 M type and standard light aircraft emergency practices. Numerical limitations are deliberately absent and must be supplied from the aircraft's own POH.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, or other numerical limitations. Best glide speed, engine-out approach speed, and other critical values must come from the aircraft POH before this file can be used as a working emergency checklist.
Emergency procedures only. Normal operating procedures are in cessna-150m-normal.
Equipment variations across the 150 M production run may add or remove items. Verify against the specific aircraft and its POH.

rights.notes: The Cessna 150 M Pilot's Operating Handbook remains under copyright. This file does not reproduce its wording, its selection of emergency items, or its arrangement.

sections.title: Engine Failure on Takeoff (At or Before Liftoff)
sections.condition: Engine fails or loses significant power during the takeoff roll or immediately after liftoff

items.text: Brakes — if still on the runway, apply firmly to stop on remaining runway
Do NOT attempt to return to the runway from a low-altitude engine failure. Land ahead or in the best available area within approximately 30 degrees either side of the nose.
Land straight ahead — use flaps if altitude and airspeed permit; brace for impact

sections.title: Engine Failure in Flight
sections.condition: Complete or partial loss of engine power after takeoff with altitude available

items.text: Select a suitable landing area within gliding range
If engine does not restart, proceed to Forced Landing checklist. Squawk 7700 and transmit MAYDAY on 121.5 MHz if time permits.

sections.title: Engine Fire in Flight
sections.condition: Flames or smoke visible from the engine compartment during flight

items.response: FULL OPEN (to consume fuel in lines)

items.text: Airspeed — increase to blow out fire if conditions allow
items.response: INCREASE — DO NOT EXCEED VNE PER POH

items.text: Execute immediate emergency landing — squawk 7700 and transmit MAYDAY if time permits

sections.title: Engine Fire on Ground (During Start)
sections.condition: Engine fire occurs during start or while engine is running on the ground

items.response: CONTINUE CRANKING to draw fire back into engine, if battery power remains
items.detail: Continued cranking may draw the fire into the induction system and extinguish it. If fire persists, proceed immediately to shutdown steps.

items.text: Evacuate aircraft immediately — use fire extinguisher if available and fire is small
Call emergency services (911) and notify airport authority

sections.title: Electrical Fire / Smoke in Cockpit
sections.condition: Smoke or burning smell from electrical system or instrument panel

items.text: If fire is extinguished and flight instruments are needed, turn master back ON and selectively restore only equipment required for safe arrival

sections.title: Loss of Oil Pressure
sections.condition: Oil pressure gauge drops below the green arc or to zero

items.text: Throttle — reduce to minimum power needed to maintain flight
Check oil pressure and oil temperature gauges — a simultaneous temperature rise confirms oil loss
Select landing area within gliding range
Low oil pressure may precede engine seizure with little additional warning. Do not delay the landing decision. Proceed to Forced Landing checklist if pressure remains low.
Proceed to Forced Landing checklist — land as soon as possible

sections.title: Carburetor Ice
sections.condition: Unexplained RPM loss or rough running on fixed-pitch engine with no other apparent cause

items.response: FULL ON — LEAVE ON UNTIL RPM RECOVERS
items.detail: Expect an initial further RPM drop as partially melted ice passes through the system. This is normal. Do not cycle the carb heat off prematurely. RPM should recover and stabilise once the ice has cleared.

items.text: Monitor RPM — an initial drop followed by recovery and smooth running confirms ice was present and is clearing

items.response: RICHEN SLIGHTLY IF NEEDED FOR ROUGH RUNNING

items.text: Once RPM stabilises, consider whether to leave carb heat on or cycle it. If icing conditions persist, leave ON.
If RPM does not recover after applying full carburetor heat, the cause may be other than icing. Treat as partial engine failure and prepare for a precautionary landing.

sections.title: Forced Landing (Power-Off)
sections.condition: Engine cannot be restarted; landing must be made without power

items.text: Airspeed — establish and maintain best glide
Select landing area — prefer open fields into the wind; assess surface, obstructions, and slope
Squawk 7700 and transmit MAYDAY on 121.5 MHz: aircraft type, position, altitude, intentions, souls on board
Flaps — extend on final to steepen approach and reduce touchdown speed
Aim to land at the slowest safe airspeed; touch down with as little groundspeed as possible and brace for deceleration
